slides.notes: Persona 1 is the lead persona. It targets the buyer who is already halfway to the close, so the ad's job is arithmetic, not persuasion.
Four buyers, four different reasons for stalling. One campaign has to speak to the average of them, which is nobody. This slide is the argument for persona specific creative.
July sold a discount to strangers. August sells a landowner an argument about the thing they already own, and only then hands them the money.
Pushback worth having: these are four objections, not four audiences, and Housing category targeting cannot separate them. I would run them as a sequenced set against one geo pool.

Three recommendations before the creative. Persona specific campaigns per market rather than one general campaign. Imagery gets replaced once we have access to the full library. And a fifth campaign for buyers without land, which needs different messaging and is in progress.

The carousel already is a funnel in one unit. Card one is awareness, two to four are consideration, card five is decision. So the journey should sequence the assets we have rather than multiply the campaigns. Decision stage retargeting on Meta needs verifying against Housing category rules.
This buyer is already halfway to the close. The message asks them to reappraise an asset they already hold, which is arithmetic rather than aspiration.
Card one never says a dollar amount. Land is the hook, the qualifier, and the thing no competitor can answer.

Five things I need before the rest of the campaign can be finished.
